scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
cards.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You owe me lunch money. Bring back ten minutes of yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I'd buy lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said anything. I kept the word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't travel through time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll need to start earlier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy your lunch today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Use that time to retrieve yesterday's minutes. Then we're square.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 mentions lunch money, but A3 justifies the demand through 'You said anything' rather than the past favor's fair value.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 responds to B2's limited offer; A5's 'start earlier' sidesteps B4's inability to travel through time.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers lunch and B4 states a limit, providing a credible debtor's resistance.

heightening.evidence: A5 supplies a time pun without increasing the repayment obligation or its practical consequences.

specificity.evidence: A1 names lunch money but gives no reason A wants those particular ten minutes of yesterday.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 is concise, while A5's detachable 'start earlier' joke weakens the exchange's specific logic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes yesterday's lunch sufficient grounds for retrieving elapsed time; A5 presents that impossible repayment as settling accounts.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes B2's sandwich repayment from lost time; A5 repurposes B4's queueing offer into time retrieval.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer increasingly relevant compensation, giving A actual solutions to reinterpret.

heightening.evidence: A5 recruits today's queueing into the demand, but mostly restates A1's unchanged ten-minute debt.

specificity.evidence: A1's lunch queue and ten minutes make the impossible claim concrete, though the present setting remains light.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's sandwich/time distinction is economical; A5's 'Then we're square' sustains the sincere fairness claim.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers lunch; A3 credits only the sandwich and keeps the elapsed-time debt outstanding.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers queueing time; A5 assigns that offered time to recovering yesterday's minutes.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats a modest favor as justification for an impossible but supposedly balanced repayment.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 converts a helpful offer into an assigned method of satisfying the original impossible debt.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A values a concrete past favor as sufficient payment for an impossible return and calmly treats that accounting as fair.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Enforcing an impossible promise would make B's wording the source of obligation instead of A's earlier kindness.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 relies on 'anything'; revised A3 divides the sandwich from the time debt and A5 calls impossible repayment square.

records.recommendedEdit: Removed the promise-based justification while preserving lunch and yesterday's time. B2 produces itemized accounting; B4's queueing offer becomes work time for the miracle. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1/A3 ground fairness in the favor), logic 5 (A3 uses lunch; A5 uses queueing), relationship 4 (B offers two remedies), heightening 4 (A5 assigns the remedy to impossible collection), specificity 5 (A1 identifies the lost minutes), brevity/wit 4 (A5's 'square' completes the accounting); total 92. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed for a narrow internal pass. A5 changes the proposed means more than the scale or consequence.
records.writerReservation: The unchanged transfer still privileges an 'anything' promise, so its provenance cannot be safely rebound to this corrected mechanism.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a exploits two practical repayment offers; b relies on moral pressure and comparative effort, with less final development.

cards.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
cards.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I helped move your sofa. Move the moon away from my window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those aren't equivalent favours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa had stairs. The moon's already airborne.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How would I do it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I didn't ask how heavy the sofa was before helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I helped move your sofa. Move the moon away from my window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those aren't equivalent favours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa had stairs. The moon's already airborne.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll move your bed away from the window. I have twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move the moon for twenty minutes each night. I didn't leave your sofa halfway upstairs.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 exchanges sofa-moving for moon-moving; A3 sincerely argues that stairs make the past favor harder.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's equivalence objection; A5 uses B4's procedural question to demand reciprocal unquestioning help.

relationship.evidence: B2 disputes the debt's scale and B4 seeks a method, allowing A to switch from comparison to obligation.

heightening.evidence: A5 raises the moral demand from equivalent labor to helping without prior investigation.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies sofa, moon and window; A3 adds stairs as the precise basis for A's accounting.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'already airborne' earns its joke through the moving comparison, and A5 sustains that same logic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes moving a sofa grounds for moving the moon; A3 sincerely balances stairs against airborne convenience, presenting the impossible repayment as fair.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 disputes equivalence, prompting A3's comparison of physical effort. B4 offers twenty minutes, which A5 converts into a nightly lunar obligation.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges the debt calculation; B4 offers practical help with the bed and a time limit, giving B a credible helpful boundary.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's finite availability into recurring service and invokes finishing the sofa move to justify completing the impossible repayment.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies the past sofa move and present window problem; B4's bed-moving offer makes the domestic situation immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'already airborne' compresses A's unfair accounting neatly; A5's 'halfway upstairs' earns its return through the original favor.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 calls the favors inequivalent; A3 supplies a sincere effort comparison intended to prove equivalence.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers bed relocation within twenty minutes. A5 adopts that duration while redirecting the help to nightly moon relocation.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 consistently treat one completed sofa-moving favor as sufficient payment for impossible labor.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 expands the original lunar request into a recurring obligation without abandoning the sofa debt.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats moving a sofa as fair consideration for moving the moon and uses the favor's difficulty to defend the exchange.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General entitlement could demand a miracle without identifying a prior favor or arguing reciprocal fairness.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 explicitly names the sofa favor; A3 compares physical effort and revised A5 uses completing that favor to justify recurring moon-moving.

records.recommendedEdit: Corrected the rejected candidate's repeated justification while preserving the sofa and moon setting. B4 now offers a practical bed move and a time limit; A5 applies that limit to recurring impossible repayment, increasing B's obligation through A's sincere fairness accounting. The saved firstPass remains unchanged and rates the original. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5 (A1/A3/A5 ground the exchange in the sofa favor), logic 5 (A3 answers B2's equivalence objection; A5 uses B4's twenty minutes), relationship 4 (B4 offers help within limited availability), heightening 4 (A5 turns one move into nightly service), specificity 4 (A1's window and B4's bed establish the domestic problem), brevity/wit 4 (A3's airborne comparison and A5's halfway-upstairs argument follow reciprocal labor); total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all hard gates pass. This is an internal model reread, with no live testing.
records.remainingConcern: A5's nightly schedule is a slightly convenient expansion of B4's one-time availability, but its opportunistic accounting remains clear. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5 extends the favor into recurring service without specifying when repayment ends; that selective accounting must sound fair to A. The unchanged S152 transfer's promise-based provenance remains incompatible.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved lunch alternative distinguishes sandwich repayment from lost time and absorbs a helpful queueing offer. This alternative argues comparative effort and converts a friend's limited availability into recurring labor.
